$comment: Per-part corrections, for parts whose filename disagrees with their model.
Every entry here was found by packages/indexer/src/audit.ts and confirmed
in two dimensions: a correction is only made when the measured height
matches one unit count *and* the measured width independently matches
another. A height that merely looks wrong is not enough, because a bbox
can legitimately exceed the mounting plate — see `perPart` in families.json.
Ten of 541 parts, all in the community-contributed Tool_hooks. The
seventeen curated families audit clean, which is the strongest evidence
yet that the parametric model holds.

parts.name: 6x4 RD6006P_Power_Supply
parts.reason: both wrong: measures 101.4 tall (h=4) and 183.2 wide (w=7)

parts.name: 3x1 Halder Secural
parts.reason: both wrong: measures 50.6 tall (h=2) and 81.6 wide (w=3)

parts.name: 1x3 Dewalt DCV501 Stick Vacuum
parts.reason: measures 50.6 tall (h=2); the width of 73.8 already agrees with w=3

parts.name: 2x3 6x 6mm Finger Slots
parts.reason: measures 25.2 tall (h=1); the width of 81.6 already agrees with w=3

parts.name: 2x6 12x 6mm Finger Slots
parts.reason: measures 25.2 tall (h=1); the width of 157.8 already agrees with w=6

notCorrected.name: 8x2.25 LiitoKala Charger
notCorrected.reason: Width 208.6 agrees with w=8, but the height of 57.0 fits no whole unit count - the nearest, h=2, is 6.4 mm out. Its name is probably height x width reversed with a fractional height, which the grid has no way to express. Left alone rather than guessed at.

notCorrected.name: 1x6 11pc Wrench Hanger
notCorrected.reason: Measures 159.1 tall against 25.2 for h=1, and Tool_hooks/README.md says to print it with 6x0 Flats. But the excess is the eleven downward hooks, not a wrong name - the bounding box exceeds the mounting plate. That is the `perPart` problem, not an override.
